components.name: Flash Controller

components.name: Channel 0...Channel D / Die 0...Die D / Plane 0...Plane P (Block 0, Page 0)
components.role: flash backbone's physical hierarchy: 8-16 channels, each with several dies, each divisible into planes, blocks and pages, over an NV-DDR interface

components.name: Upper-layer Software (e.g., Block Layer)
components.role: host-side software issuing an I/O Request

components.name: NVMe Driver
components.role: host driver that submits NVMe commands to a submission queue and rings its doorbell

components.name: Queue Pair (QP)
components.role: submission/completion queue pair used by the NVMe driver

components.name: SSD Firmware
components.role: firmware running the device-side I/O path from doorbell to flash operation

components.name: SQ Tail Fetch
components.role: fetches NVMe commands from the submission queue via the host interface controller

components.name: DMA Engine
components.role: performs the host-SSD data transfer (DMA OP) for the command

components.name: Parse & Slice
components.role: parses the NVMe command and slices it into 4KB units

components.name: Address Translation
components.role: translates LPN to PPN via the cached mapping table (Directory + Cache Lookup)

content.key_idea: A traditional JBOF pairs a DPU host with many independent SSDs over PCIe; each SSD's own ARM-based firmware independently fetches, parses, translates, DMAs, and flashes every NVMe I/O end-to-end, with no sharing of computing resources across SSDs.
content.reading_order: Panel (a) top-left: DPU host to SSDs over PCIe. Panel (b) bottom-left: one SSD's controller and flash backbone. Panel (c) right: the numbered NVMe I/O path through that SSD's firmware.

summary: This figure details the traditional JBOF system that the paper's own design (Espresso) targets, in three panels. (a) A JBOF pairs a DPU host, containing NIC/HCA, ARM Processor, DRAM, DDR Ctrl. and a PCIe Root Complex, with tens of SSDs (SSD 0...SSD n) over a PCIe Interconnection. (b) Each SSD's controller integrates a Host Interface Controller, an ARM Processor running firmware (command parsing, address translation, GC/wear-leveling), a DMA Engine, and DRAM caching a mapping table, all coupled through a Flash Controller to a flash backbone of channels, dies, planes, blocks and pages. (c) A zoomed, numbered I/O path shows an NVMe Driver's request ringing a doorbell (1-2), the SSD firmware fetching (3), parsing/slicing (4), translating LPN to PPN (5), DMA-transferring (6), and finally issuing the flash command (7).
summary_zh: 该图分三部分展示传统 JBOF 架构：(a) DPU 主机经 PCIe 接多块 SSD；(b) SSD 控制器含 ARM 固件、DMA 引擎与映射表缓存，经闪存控制器接闪存阵列；(c) 编号展示 NVMe I/O 路径各步骤。
notes: The index marks this figure's role as 'motivation' (section 2, Background and Motivation): it depicts the traditional/baseline JBOF-SSD-NVMe architecture that Espresso's design targets, not Espresso's own novel mechanism, so all components are marked novel:false. The given body text is truncated right after step 7, so the completion path (flash controller back to host doorbell/CQ) shown in the figure is not independently confirmed by the provided text. layout-proposal: multi-panel teardown — two small overview diagrams (JBOF architecture, SSD architecture) paired with one large numbered I/O-path pipeline detail panel in an L-shaped/2x2 grid; no single named template captures an overview+detail-pipeline teardown like this.
